description: Governed, multi-tenant, MCP-native builder for agents, RAG and workflows. Adopt LangGraph/LlamaIndex/LiteLLM/pgvector/MCP; build the governance (versioned manifest + 4 seams). Foundation (seams, manifest schema, scaffold, CI) is already committed; these stories build the modules on top.

userStories.title: Manifest versioning: diff + rollback + store
userStories.description: As a builder, I need immutable published manifest versions with diff and rollback so agent config is IaC.
acceptanceCriteria: core/manifest/versioning.py: publish(draft)->immutable version (monotonic), diff(v_a,v_b) via deepdiff, rollback(id,version)->new version copying an older one
core/manifest/store.py: in-memory ManifestStore (tenant-scoped) with save/get/list/history; Protocol so a DB store swaps in later
Published versions cannot be mutated (publish creates a new version; draft edits allowed only pre-publish)
Unit tests offline: publish increments version, diff shows changed fields, rollback creates new version equal to target payload, tenant isolation enforced
ruff check . clean and pytest -q green
userStories.notes: Build on core/manifest/schema.py (AgentManifest). Everything tenant-scoped via TenantContext. | DONE: merged via PR.

userStories.title: Agent runtime via LangGraph (1 model + 1 tool, governed)
userStories.description: As a user, I run an agent from its manifest: it calls a model and a tool and answers, with governance enforced.
acceptanceCriteria: core/runtime/agent.py implements AgentRuntime.run(manifest,message,tenant)->RunResult using LangGraph (StateGraph: model node <-> tool node loop)

Model calls ONLY via ModelProvider seam; tools ONLY via ToolProvider seam; every model/tool checked through AuthzProvider against manifest allow-lists (denied ones recorded in RunResult.denied, never invoked)
TenantContext threaded through every node (use_tenant)
Guardrails applied (max_tool_calls, temperature, system_suffix)
Offline test using EchoModelProvider + InMemoryToolProvider: agent invokes an allowed tool and returns; a non-allowed tool is denied not called
Degrades gracefully if langgraph missing (import guarded) but real path uses LangGraph; ruff clean, pytest green offline
userStories.notes: Hardest core module. Keep the graph small. RunResult contract is fixed in core/runtime/__init__.py. | DONE: merged via PR.

userStories.title: RAG: LlamaIndex + pgvector behind RagIndex, cited retrieval
userStories.description: As a user, I ingest docs and the agent retrieves chunks with citations, tenant-isolated.
acceptanceCriteria: core/rag/llamaindex_pgvector.py implements RagIndex (ingest/retrieve) using LlamaIndex + pgvector; collections namespaced by tenant_id (no cross-tenant leakage)
core/rag/memory.py: an in-memory RagIndex (embedding-free, keyword/overlap scoring) so examples+tests run offline with zero deps
retrieve returns RetrievedChunk with source+score+metadata for citation
Factory core/rag/factory.py picks memory impl when AGENT_STUDIO_OFFLINE=1 or pgvector unavailable, else pgvector
Offline tests: ingest N docs, retrieve returns relevant chunk with source; tenant A cannot see tenant B docs
ruff clean, pytest green offline (pgvector path guarded/skipped when no DB)
userStories.notes: RagIndex Protocol fixed in core/rag/__init__.py. pgvector integration test may be skipped without DATABASE_URL. | DONE: merged via PR.

userStories.title: Workflows: multi-step + multi-agent + human-in-the-loop
userStories.description: As a user, I run a workflow triage->specialist->human-review that pauses for approval and resumes.
acceptanceCriteria: core/workflows/graph.py implements WorkflowEngine.start/resume using LangGraph with a durable interrupt for human-in-the-loop (WAITING_APPROVAL state + pending_step)
Definition is declarative dict (steps: agent|condition|human_approval, edges); conditional branching supported
resume(run_id, approval) continues a paused run to completion
Steps that run agents go through the runtime contract (accept an injected runner) so workflows stay decoupled from US-002 internals
Offline test: start a 3-step workflow, assert it pauses at human_approval, resume with approve, assert COMPLETED; reject path branches
ruff clean, pytest green offline
userStories.notes: WorkflowEngine contract fixed in core/workflows/__init__.py. Inject the agent runner to avoid a hard dep on US-002. | DONE: merged via PR.

userStories.title: Builder UI (React + shadcn, minimal) over the API
userStories.description: As a builder, I create/edit an agent, attach RAG sources, assemble a workflow and run it, in a minimal UI.
acceptanceCriteria: builder/ Vite + React + TS + Tailwind + shadcn/ui scaffold that builds (pnpm build)
Screens: Agents list, Agent editor (name, system prompt, model, allowed tools, RAG sources), Run panel (send message, show answer + citations + denials), Workflow runner (start, approve/reject)
Typed API client in builder/src/lib/api.ts targeting the FastAPI contract (agents CRUD, run, ingest, versions, workflows); base URL from VITE_API_URL
Uses a mock/fixture layer so the UI renders without a live backend (MSW or a simple fetch shim toggled by VITE_USE_MOCKS)
pnpm build succeeds; README in builder/ explains dev + mock mode
eslint clean
userStories.notes: Frontend only; treat the API as a contract (ADR-0004 API-first). Independent of Python stories. | DONE: merged via PR.

userStories.title: FastAPI routers: agents CRUD, run, ingest, versions, workflows
userStories.description: As an integrator, I drive the whole system over HTTP.
acceptanceCriteria: api/routers/{agents,runs,ingest,versions,workflows}.py mounted in api/main.py

Endpoints: POST/GET/PUT /agents, POST /agents/{id}/publish, GET /agents/{id}/versions, POST /agents/{id}/rollback, POST /agents/{id}/run, POST /sources/{name}/ingest, POST /workflows/run, POST /workflows/{id}/resume
TenantContext resolved from X-Tenant-Id header (default tenant when absent) and threaded into every call
Pydantic request/response models; wired to core stores/runtime/rag/workflows via the seams (EchoModelProvider + memory impls when AGENT_STUDIO_OFFLINE=1)
FastAPI TestClient tests offline for each endpoint (happy path + a governance-denied tool case)
ruff clean, pytest green offline
userStories.notes: Depends on wave 1 modules being merged to main first. | DONE: merged via PR.

userStories.title: CLI subcommands (agent create/run, ingest, versions)
userStories.description: As a developer, I drive core flows from the terminal.
acceptanceCriteria: api/cli.py Typer commands: agent create/list/show/run, source ingest, version list/diff/rollback
Reads/writes through the same core stores as the API (shared, not duplicated)
Offline by default (AGENT_STUDIO_OFFLINE=1)
CliRunner tests for create+run+ingest happy paths
ruff clean, pytest green
userStories.notes: Depends on wave 1. Reuse API service layer where possible. | DONE: merged via PR.

userStories.title: Examples: 1 agent + 1 RAG + 1 workflow that run out of the box
userStories.description: As a new user, `make examples` runs all 3 demos with no code edits and no API key.
acceptanceCriteria: examples/agent_demo.py: manifest-defined agent uses a tool and answers
examples/rag_demo.py: ingest sample docs, agent answers citing sources
examples/workflow_demo.py: triage->specialist->human review, auto-approves in demo, runs end to end
examples/run_all.py runs all three and prints results; `python -m examples.run_all` works
All run offline (EchoModelProvider + memory RAG); Makefile `examples` target works
ruff clean; a smoke test asserts run_all completes
userStories.notes: Depends on wave 1. This is DoD item: git clone && make dev runs the 3 examples. | DONE: merged via PR.

userStories.title: Governance v0 end-to-end + seams documentation
userStories.description: As a platform owner, governance filters tools/models/sources by manifest, tenant threaded everywhere, documented.
acceptanceCriteria: End-to-end test: an agent whose manifest omits a tool is denied that tool at runtime AND via the API; a disallowed model is refused
TenantContext demonstrably isolates data/vectors across two tenants in one test
docs/seams.md documents the 4 seams, current stub vs future target, and how to swap implementations
docs/governance.md explains manifest allow-lists as the enforced surface
ruff clean, pytest green offline
userStories.notes: Ties the governance story together. Depends on runtime + API merged. | DONE: merged via PR.
